text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Istvan Nikolits, minister in charge of civil secret services said he does not feel any responsibility for the fact the Intelligence Office gathered information on several MPs through unlawful means in late 1994 or early 1995. After a fact-finding investigation he informed Parliament's national security committee. Two agents have been dismissed.

- Parliament Tuesday amended the tax and social insurance regulations to exempt farmers from having to file a tax return if their annual sales revenue is under HUF 1 million and if they have receipts for 20 percent of that figure. Farmers dissatisfied with the decision will roll out their vehicles from Kiskoros today at the call of the Agricultural Producer Advocacy Organisation and try to slow down traffic.

- In its presentation at the International Court of Justice yesterday Slovakia strove to refute the argument that Hungary was forced to terminate the construction of the Gabcikovo - Nagymaros hydropower plants because an environmental emergency existed.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs will visit Egypt April 1-2 to explore ways of promoting economic cooperation.

- A State Audit Office report found that the State Privatisation and Holding Co. violated the privatisation law by selling state companies without including a capital increase and development in sales contracts.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The European Union's bank the European Investment Bank will held its board of directors meeting in Budapest next month.
- Romanian President Emil Constantinescu and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will receive Democratic Forum president Sandor Lezsak in Bucharest today.
- The National Police are organising a railway police force to start work next year.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The Federation of Hungarian Jewish Communities said in a letter to Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal Tuesday that Deputy Speaker Agnes Nagy Maczo is unfit to hold that high public position in Parliament.

- The live pig market was unusually active in the first few months of the year, as meat processors purchased nearly 20 percent more pigs than in the same period of last year. A new swine disease has been spreading in Hungary in the last few months.
- Individuals' foreign exchange savings continued to drop in February, National Bank of Hungary figures reveal.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- The foreign trade balance is expected to deteriorate by $500 million this year compared to last year, due to a 10-12 percent projected increase in imports, said Deputy State Secretary at the Ministry of Industry Lajos Berenyi.
- Individuals hold more than HUF 30 billion in the 280 pension funds operating in Hungary at present.
- K&H Bank plans to issue subordinated loan capital bonds to a total value of $30 million with a maturity period of seven years.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- According to the coordinated version of the new corporate law expected to take effect next January, the minimum capital required to found a limited company will be HUF 3 million.
